title: Natural Leray spectral sequence for module sheaves on ringed sites
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to a common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C},\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$. Let $f$ be a morphism of their ringed topoi: a geometric morphism $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$, with $f^{-1}$ preserving finite limits, together with a ring map $f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}\to\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$. Use the induced module direct image (the underlying abelian direct image with this scalar action) on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $H^n(\mathcal C,-)$ and $H^n(\mathcal D,-)$ for right-derived global sections in the respective module categories, and $R^qf_*$ for right-derived module direct image, all computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. For every $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-module $F$ there is a first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence, natural in module maps $F\to F'$, with
$$E_2^{a,b}=H^a(\mathcal D,R^bf_*F)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad H^{a+b}(\mathcal C,F).$$
Convergence means that for each $n\geq0$ the abutment has a finite decreasing filtration $H^n=\mathrm{Fil}^0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq\mathrm{Fil}^{n+1}=0$ whose graded pieces are $\mathrm{Fil}^a/\mathrm{Fil}^{a+1}\cong E_\infty^{a,n-a}$. The natural edge map $H^n(\mathcal C,F)\to H^0(\mathcal D,R^nf_*F)$ is the composite of the quotient to $E_\infty^{0,n}$ and its canonical inclusion into $E_2^{0,n}$. For an injective module resolution $F\to I^\bullet$, it sends a global cocycle of $I^\bullet$ to its image in the sections of $\mathcal H^n(f_*I^\bullet)=R^nf_*F$. It is independent of the resolution. No flatness of the ring map or exactness of module tensor pullback is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0732, lemma-Leray, applied to F in degree zero; Tag 0733(2), lemma-apply-Leray, for the edge; derived.tex Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence, for functoriality and the abutment filtration.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$. These are Grothendieck abelian by the arbitrary-ring-sheaf theorem and have enough injectives by the Grothendieck enough-injectives theorem. The same arbitrary-ring-sheaf theorem on the punctual site with ring $\mathbf Z$ gives the required Grothendieck property for $\mathrm{Ab}$: a module sheaf there is one abelian group with its unique integer scalar action. Work throughout in the common coefficient universe.

Set $P=f_*:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G=\Gamma(\mathcal D,-):\mathcal B\to\mathrm{Ab}$. The module adjunction makes $P$ a right adjoint: the adjunction identifies maps into $P(\ker v)$ with maps into $\ker P(v)$, giving preservation of kernels. Its underlying maps preserve addition by the ringed-topos module-action definition. For $G$, kernels and sums of maps are computed on sections, so $G$ is additive left exact as well. On underlying sets the sheaf adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(1,f_*M)=\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}1,M)=\operatorname{Hom}(1,M)$, since $f^{-1}$ preserves the terminal object. This bijection respects addition and module morphisms. Hence $GP\cong\Gamma(\mathcal C,-)$ naturally, including the differentials on complexes.

For every injective $I\in\mathcal A$, the injective-pushforward acyclicity lemma gives $R^pG(P I)=0$ for $p>0$. Thus $(P,G)$ satisfies exactly the composable-pair acyclicity condition. This supplies the hypothesis needed for the Grothendieck spectral sequence without asserting that $PI$ is injective or that module pullback is exact.

Apply the general Grothendieck spectral sequence to $(P,G)$ and the degree-zero object $F$. It gives, functorially in $F$, $E_2^{a,b}=R^aG(R^bP(F))=H^a(\mathcal D,R^bf_*F)$ for $a,b\geq0$. Its abutment is $R^{a+b}(GP)(F)$, identified by the natural isomorphism of step 2 with $H^{a+b}(\mathcal C,F)$. By the double-complex model lemma, for an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ and a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution $C^{\bullet,\bullet}$ of $P I^\bullet$, this spectral sequence with its abutment filtration is the spectral sequence of the filtration of $\operatorname{Tot}G(C^{\bullet,\bullet})$ named there, with $E_2^{a,b}=R^aG(R^bP(F))$; use this model to fix the filtration and edges.

Apply the double-complex convergence theorem to that filtration of the first-quadrant double complex $G(C^{\bullet,\bullet})$ of step 4. In total degree $n$, only the $n+1$ bidegrees $(a,n-a)$ with $0\leq a\leq n$ occur. Its image filtration therefore has $\mathrm{Fil}^0=H^n$, $\mathrm{Fil}^{n+1}=0$, and $\mathrm{Fil}^a/\mathrm{Fil}^{a+1}\cong E_\infty^{a,n-a}$. This theorem also gives stabilization and functoriality of these filtrations under the comparison maps used in the functorial Grothendieck construction.

The double-complex model for the Grothendieck left edge identifies it with $H^n\twoheadrightarrow\mathrm{Fil}^0/\mathrm{Fil}^1=E_\infty^{0,n}\hookrightarrow E_2^{0,n}$. In column zero there are no incoming differentials on pages $r\geq2$, so each later column-zero term is a subobject of the previous one; this explains the stated inclusion into $E_2^{0,n}=G(R^nP(F))$. The general cocycle description of this same edge sends a cocycle in $G(P I^\bullet)$ through $G(Z^n(P I^\bullet))\to G(\mathcal H^n(P I^\bullet))$. Under $GP I^\bullet=\Gamma(\mathcal C,I^\bullet)$, this is exactly the global-cocycle formula in the item, with $\mathcal H^n(P I^\bullet)=R^nf_*F$.

source.place: Tag 015N, lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence, Cartan--Eilenberg construction of the left edge

proof.text: The cocycle theorem describes the canonical Grothendieck edge for any chosen injective resolution, using the canonical derived-functor comparisons. The derived well-definedness lemma makes those identifications independent of the chosen resolution. Consequently the displayed formula computes one resolution-independent edge, and the functoriality in $F$ of the Grothendieck sequence makes it natural in every module map $F\to F'$. This proves all the assertions with the original hypotheses.

tool_uses.why: The general ring-sheaf category theorem supplies the Grothendieck input; this unit has no separate proof of this generic fact.
The generic enough-injectives implication supplies resolutions for the module categories.
The generic module adjunction gives left exactness of the module direct image on arbitrary ringed topoi.
The general composable-pair theorem constructs the Leray sequence after the specific acyclicity hypothesis is checked.
The generic first-quadrant convergence theorem supplies the finite image filtration.
The generic model fixes the left edge as the quotient to the stable term followed by its inclusion.
